query: What is the transmissibility formula?
ground_truth: Transmitted G formula: GT = (2*pi*fn*V)/g, where fn is natural frequency in Hz, V is velocity change (1.0791 m/s for the standard 20G/11ms saw-tooth pulse), g is 9.81 m/s^2. For the worked example (CB1400-15, 850 kg, 6 bottom + 4 wall, m=141.67 kg, fn=9.109 Hz): GT = 6.296 G. [source: formulas.md]

query: How do I calculate natural frequency of a mount?
ground_truth: Natural frequency formula: fn = (1/(2*pi)) * sqrt(k/m) in Hz, where k is isolator stiffness in N/m and m is mass per isolator in kg. Example for CB1400-15 at 141.67 kg: k = 464086 N/m, fn = 9.109 Hz. [source: formulas.md]

query: Static deflection equation
ground_truth: Dynamic deflection formula: dD = V / (2*pi*fn) in meters, multiplied by 1000 to convert to mm. For the 20G/11ms saw-tooth pulse V = 1.0791 m/s, so dD (mm) = 1000 * 1.0791 / (2*pi*fn). Worked example with fn = 9.109 Hz gives dD = 18.85 mm. [source: formulas.md]

query: Compression bottom load case mass distribution
ground_truth: Comp-Bottom load case: mass per isolator m = M / n_bottom (no /2 factor, because vertical gravity acts on all bottom mounts equally and simultaneously). For M = 850 kg with n_bottom = 6: m = 141.67 kg. Direction Z, vertical, uses K_compression and dmax_comp. [source: load_cases.md]

query: Why divide by 2 in the roll wall case?
ground_truth: The /2 factor in Roll-Wall (and the other lateral cases): lateral shock is resisted simultaneously by mounts on both opposing sides of the structure, so each side carries half the load: m = M / n_wall / 2. This convention is from the validated Excel template; omitting it doubles the per-isolator mass and gives wrong GT and dD. Only the vertical Comp-Bottom case has NO /2 because gravity is unidirectional. [source: load_cases.md]

query: Rule for picking the softest valid spring
ground_truth: Selection rule: among all parts that pass GT < GT_limit AND dD < dmax across all 4 load cases, pick the part with the LOWEST K_compression. Reason: fn = (1/2pi)*sqrt(K/m) is monotonically increasing in K, and GT = (2*pi*fn*V)/g is monotonically increasing in fn, so softer K means lower GT means better isolation. [source: selection_rules.md]

query: CB1500 stiffness values
ground_truth: CB1500 family (5/8 inch wire rope, 6 variants): CB1500-12 K_comp=5375 lb/in K_shear=2735, CB1500-15 K_comp=3655 K_shear=1870, CB1500-20 K_comp=2585 K_shear=1250, CB1500-30 K_comp=1610 K_shear=800, CB1500-40 K_comp=1155 K_shear=560, CB1500-50 K_comp=795 K_shear=410. dmax_comp ranges from 1.2 to 3.2 inches. Source: Helical CB 1500 Series datasheet. [source: catalog_overview.md]

query: Maximum allowable deflection for CB1800
ground_truth: CB1800 is not in the official Helical catalog -- it has been replaced by CB1700 (7/8 inch wire). CB1700 dmax_comp values: CB1700-15 = 2.0 in, CB1700-17 = 2.4 in, CB1700-20 = 2.8 in, CB1700-30 = 3.6 in, CB1700-40 = 4.0 in. [source: catalog_overview.md]

query: whats the difference between CB1400 and CB1500 which one for heavier rack
ground_truth: CB1400 vs CB1500: CB1400 uses 1/2 inch wire rope (suitable load range ~200-1000 kg, standard 19 inch racks). CB1500 uses 5/8 inch wire rope (heavier construction, suitable load range ~500-1800 kg, heavy 19 inch racks). For heavier racks above ~1000 kg, CB1500 has the higher capacity envelope. [source: catalog_overview.md]

query: how do i know if the isolator i picked is actually valid for my design
ground_truth: Pass condition: an isolator is valid only when ALL 4 load cases pass both GT < GT_limit (typically 10G) AND dD < dmax (compression or shear travel from datasheet). The 4 cases are Comp-Bottom (Z), Comp-Wall (Y), Roll-Wall (XZ), Roll-Bottom (XY). If any one of the 4 fails, the part is not acceptable. [source: selection_rules.md]

query: none of the CB parts pass for my mass what do i do
ground_truth: When NO part passes, in order of preference: (1) increase mount count (n_bottom and/or n_wall) -- lowers mass per isolator, lowers fn, lowers GT. (2) Relax GT_limit if the protected equipment can actually tolerate higher G. (3) Re-evaluate the shock profile (confirm Ao and to with the project spec). (4) Move up a series -- CB1500 (5/8 in rope) or CB1700 (7/8 in rope) have higher capacity. [source: selection_rules.md]

query: do i need to divide by 2 for the bottom z-axis compression case
ground_truth: No -- Comp-Bottom (Z-axis vertical) has NO /2 factor. Mass per isolator is m = M / n_bottom only. The /2 applies only to the three lateral cases (Comp-Wall Y, Roll-Wall XZ, Roll-Bottom XY) because two opposing sides share lateral load. Vertical gravity is unidirectional, so all bottom mounts carry weight simultaneously. [source: load_cases.md]

query: give me the equation for transmitted G
ground_truth: Transmitted G: GT = (2*pi*fn*V) / g, where fn is natural frequency in Hz, V is velocity change in m/s (1.0791 m/s for 20G/11ms saw-tooth), g = 9.81 m/s^2. The pass condition is GT < GT_limit (typically 10G, set by equipment fragility). [source: formulas.md]

query: i have K in lb/in how do i convert it to N/m
ground_truth: Unit conversion: 1 lb/in = 175.1268 N/m. Example: K_comp for CB1400-15 = 2650 lb/in * 175.1268 = 464086 N/m. Also 1 in = 25.4 mm, so dmax_comp 1.4 in = 35.56 mm. These conversions are applied automatically inside CatalogEntry.to_isolator_spec(). [source: catalog_overview.md]

query: what shock pulse is this whole analysis based on
ground_truth: Shock profile: 20G magnitude (Ao), 11 ms duration (to), saw-tooth pulse. Corresponds to MIL-STD-810H Category 4 (off-road wheeled vehicle). Velocity change V = 0.5 * g * Ao * to = 1.0791 m/s for this pulse. [source: formulas.md]

query: formula for transmitted G and which load cases have the divide by 2
ground_truth: GT formula: GT = (2*pi*fn*V)/g [source: formulas.md]. The /2 factor applies to the lateral cases -- Comp-Wall (Y), Roll-Wall (XZ), Roll-Bottom (XY) -- where two opposing sides resist lateral shock together. Only Comp-Bottom (Z, vertical) has NO /2 because gravity is unidirectional. [source: load_cases.md]

query: for an 850 kg rack with 6 bottom 4 wall whats the per-isolator mass and how to pick spring
ground_truth: Per-isolator mass for M=850 kg, n_bottom=6, n_wall=4: Comp-Bottom m = 850/6 = 141.67 kg, Comp-Wall m = 850/4/2 = 106.25 kg, Roll-Wall m = 850/4/2 = 106.25 kg, Roll-Bottom m = 850/6/2 = 70.83 kg. Selection rule: among parts passing all 4 cases (GT < GT_limit AND dD < dmax), pick the lowest K_compression. [source: load_cases.md, selection_rules.md]

query: softest spring wins rule and the dmax limits i need to check it against
ground_truth: Selection rule: among valid parts (passing all 4 cases), pick the lowest K_compression for best isolation (softer K means lower fn means lower GT). dmax to check against: each part has dmax_comp (used for Comp-Bottom and Comp-Wall cases) and dmax_shear (used for Roll-Wall and Roll-Bottom cases). Both pulled from the datasheet -- example CB1400-15: dmax_comp = 1.4 in = 35.56 mm, dmax_shear = 1.6 in = 40.64 mm. [source: selection_rules.md, catalog_overview.md]

query: natural frequency formula and which K applies to the roll wall case
ground_truth: Natural frequency: fn = (1/(2*pi)) * sqrt(K/m) in Hz. For Roll-Wall (XZ, shear direction): use K_shear (the lateral/shear deflection mode of the wire rope), NOT K_compression. Comp-Bottom and Comp-Wall use K_compression; Roll-Wall and Roll-Bottom use K_shear/roll. [source: formulas.md, load_cases.md]

query: the 4 load cases an isolator must pass and where to find dmax values
ground_truth: The 4 load cases: (1) Comp-Bottom (Z, vertical, m = M/n_bottom, K_comp, dmax_comp). (2) Comp-Wall (Y, lateral, m = M/n_wall/2, K_comp, dmax_comp). (3) Roll-Wall (XZ, shear, m = M/n_wall/2, K_shear, dmax_shear). (4) Roll-Bottom (XY, shear, m = M/n_bottom/2, K_shear, dmax_shear). dmax values live in the CB series catalog tables -- e.g. CB1400-15 dmax_comp = 1.4 in, dmax_shear = 1.6 in. [source: load_cases.md, catalog_overview.md]

query: how far can the wire mount squish before failing
ground_truth: Wire rope isolator max travel: limited by dmax_comp (compression direction) or dmax_shear (lateral direction) from the datasheet. Beyond this, the rope bottoms out and the isolator fails. Values vary by part: CB1400-15 dmax_comp = 1.4 in = 35.56 mm, dmax_shear = 1.6 in = 40.64 mm. The dynamic deflection dD = V/(2*pi*fn) must stay below these limits in every load case. [source: catalog_overview.md]

query: what makes one CB part more forgiving on impact than another
ground_truth: Softer parts (lower K_compression) give better shock isolation. Reason: fn = (1/2pi)*sqrt(K/m) is monotonic in K, and GT (transmitted shock to equipment) = (2*pi*fn*V)/g is monotonic in fn. So lower K means lower fn means lower transmitted G means equipment sees less impact. Trade-off: softer parts have larger dD (deflection), so they may exceed dmax or installation clearance. The selection rule picks the SOFTEST K that still passes all constraints. [source: selection_rules.md]

query: how to estimate how much shock energy makes it through to the equipment
ground_truth: Transmitted shock to equipment: GT (transmitted G) = (2*pi*fn*V) / g. Inputs: fn = natural frequency in Hz, V = velocity change in the shock pulse in m/s (1.0791 m/s for 20G/11ms saw-tooth), g = 9.81 m/s^2. Lower GT means less shock through. Equipment passes when GT < GT_limit (typically 10G, set by equipment fragility spec). [source: formulas.md]

query: what road conditions inform the input pulse choice
ground_truth: MIL-STD-810H Category 4 (off-road wheeled vehicle) is the source for the 20G / 11 ms saw-tooth shock profile used in this analysis. Used for sizing isolators on military vehicle-mounted shelter equipment. Ao = 20G shock magnitude, to = 0.011 s pulse duration, V = 1.0791 m/s velocity change. [source: formulas.md]

query: what gauge of cable does each series use
ground_truth: Wire rope diameter by series: CB61400 = 1/2 in (6-strand helical), CB1400 = 1/2 in (standard 6-strand), CB1500 = 5/8 in, CB1700 = 7/8 in. CB61400 has same physical dimensions as CB1400 but ~25% softer. Source: Helical datasheets supplied by supervisor. [source: catalog_overview.md]

query: 850 kg rack with 6 bottom and 4 wall mounts, which CB part should I use?
ground_truth: Recommendation: CB1400-15 in 6 bottom + 4 wall configuration (the validated Excel reference case). Per-isolator mass: Comp-Bottom = 141.67 kg, Comp-Wall = 106.25 kg, Roll-Wall = 106.25 kg, Roll-Bottom = 70.83 kg. Limiting case Comp-Bottom: fn = 9.109 Hz, GT = 6.296 G (63% of 10G limit), dD = 18.85 mm (53% of dmax_comp = 35.56 mm). Standard applied: 20G/11ms saw-tooth per MIL-STD-810H Category 4 [source: formulas.md]. Why softest: selection rule picks lowest K_comp passing all 4 cases [source: selection_rules.md].

query: 1200 kg cabinet with 4 bottom mounts and 4 wall mounts, recommend a CB part
ground_truth: Recommendation: for M = 1200 kg with 4 bottom + 4 wall mounts, the softest CB part that passes all 4 load cases. Per-isolator mass: Comp-Bottom = 300 kg (1200/4), Comp-Wall = 150 kg (1200/4/2), Roll-Wall = 150 kg, Roll-Bottom = 150 kg. Standard applied: 20G/11ms saw-tooth per MIL-STD-810H Category 4 [source: formulas.md]. Selection rule: softest K_comp that keeps GT < 10G AND dD < dmax in all 4 cases [source: selection_rules.md]. Caveat: 4+4 has fewer mounts than the typical 6+4, increasing per-isolator mass and pushing toward stiffer parts in the CB1400 or CB1500 series.

query: 200 kg lightweight rack, what mount should I use? 6 bottom + 4 wall
ground_truth: Recommendation: for M = 200 kg with 6 bottom + 4 wall mounts, a soft CB1400 variant (typically CB1400-40 to -60 region) is needed because low mass drives fn high, which drives GT high -- stiff parts often FAIL the 10G GT limit at low mass. Per-isolator mass: Comp-Bottom = 33.33 kg (200/6), Comp-Wall = 25 kg (200/4/2), Roll-Wall = 25 kg, Roll-Bottom = 16.67 kg. Standard applied: 20G/11ms saw-tooth per MIL-STD-810H Category 4 [source: formulas.md]. Caveat: at low mass, stiff parts (like CB1400-15) often FAIL on GT because fn = sqrt(K/m)/(2pi) becomes high -- softer K_comp parts are required [source: selection_rules.md].

query: Heavy 2500 kg shelter with 8 bottom and 6 wall mounts, pick a CB part
ground_truth: Recommendation: for M = 2500 kg with 8 bottom + 6 wall mounts (heavy shelter rack config), the softest CB1500 or CB1700 variant that passes all 4 cases. Per-isolator mass: Comp-Bottom = 312.5 kg (2500/8), Comp-Wall = 208.33 kg (2500/6/2), Roll-Wall = 208.33 kg, Roll-Bottom = 156.25 kg. Standard applied: 20G/11ms saw-tooth per MIL-STD-810H Category 4 [source: formulas.md]. Caveat: 2500 kg is at the upper end of CB1400 capacity range -- CB1500 (5/8 in rope, ~500-1800 kg range) or CB1700 (7/8 in rope, ~800-3000 kg range) are appropriate for this mass [source: catalog_overview.md].

query: What CB part for 600 kg rack? Just use defaults for everything else
ground_truth: Recommendation: for M = 600 kg with default 6 bottom + 4 wall mounts and default 20G/11ms shock spec, the softest CB1400 variant that passes all 4 cases (likely in the CB1400-30 to -60 region given the moderate mass). Per-isolator mass: Comp-Bottom = 100 kg (600/6), Comp-Wall = 75 kg (600/4/2), Roll-Wall = 75 kg, Roll-Bottom = 50 kg. Standard applied: 20G/11ms saw-tooth per MIL-STD-810H Category 4 [source: formulas.md]. Why softest: lowest K_comp passing all 4 cases gives the lowest transmitted G [source: selection_rules.md].

query: Verify CB1500-30 for a 1500 kg rack with default 6 bottom 4 wall config
ground_truth: CB1500-30 verification for M = 1500 kg, default 6 bottom + 4 wall, 20G/11ms shock: PASSES all 4 cases. Per-isolator mass: Comp-Bottom = 250 kg (1500/6), Comp-Wall = 187.5 kg (1500/4/2), Roll-Wall = 187.5 kg, Roll-Bottom = 125 kg. CB1500-30 has K_comp = 1610 lb/in, K_shear = 800 lb/in, dmax_comp = 2.2 in, dmax_shear = 2.2 in [source: catalog_overview.md]. Comp-Bottom GT ~3.7G (37% of 10G limit), dD ~32 mm (vs dmax_comp 55.88 mm). All 4 cases pass; worst dD ~40 mm on Roll-Wall (shear). Standard applied: 20G/11ms saw-tooth per MIL-STD-810H Category 4 [source: formulas.md].

query: Does CB1400-15 pass for 950 kg with the standard 6+4 config?
ground_truth: CB1400-15 verification for M = 950 kg, 6 bottom + 4 wall, 20G/11ms shock: ALL 4 cases PASS. Per-isolator mass: Comp-Bottom = 158.33 kg, Comp-Wall = 118.75 kg, Roll-Wall = 118.75 kg, Roll-Bottom = 79.17 kg. Comp-Bottom fn ~8.6 Hz, GT ~6.0G. Comp-Wall GT ~6.9G. Roll-Wall (K_shear) GT ~4.4G, dD ~27 mm vs dmax_shear 40.64 mm. Roll-Bottom GT ~5.4G. All under 10G limit; worst dD ~27 mm under 40.64 mm. Standard applied: 20G/11ms saw-tooth per MIL-STD-810H Category 4 [source: formulas.md]. Pass condition: GT < 10G AND dD < dmax [source: selection_rules.md].

query: Will CB1400-50 work for a 750 kg load with standard mounts?
ground_truth: CB1400-50 verification for M = 750 kg, default 6+4 mounts, 20G/11ms shock: PASSES all 4 cases. Per-isolator mass: Comp-Bottom = 125 kg, Comp-Wall = 93.75 kg, Roll-Wall = 93.75 kg, Roll-Bottom = 62.5 kg. CB1400-50 K_comp = 500 lb/in (~87563 N/m). Comp-Bottom fn ~4.2 Hz, GT ~2.9G (29% of 10G limit). Roll-Wall (K_shear) dD ~49 mm vs dmax_shear ~81.28 mm. Verdict: passes with comfortable margin; this part is appropriate for this mass. Standard applied: 20G/11ms saw-tooth per MIL-STD-810H Category 4 [source: formulas.md, selection_rules.md].

query: What's the heaviest mass that CB1400-30 can handle with 6+4 mounts?
ground_truth: CB1400-30 valid mass range with 6 bottom + 4 wall mounts, 20G/11ms shock: approximately 100-150 kg <= M <= 1800-2000 kg. Lower bound (~100 kg): below this, Comp-Bottom GT exceeds the 10G limit (mass too light makes fn high). Upper bound (~1800 kg): above this, Roll-Wall dD exceeds dmax_shear = 60.96 mm (mass too heavy makes deflection too large). The find_capacity_limit tool finds both bounds via binary search. Standard: 20G/11ms saw-tooth per MIL-STD-810H Category 4 [source: formulas.md, selection_rules.md].

query: Find the valid mass range for CB1500-50 with default mount config
ground_truth: CB1500-50 valid mass range with default 6 bottom + 4 wall mounts, 20G/11ms shock: approximately 100 kg <= M <= 3200 kg. Lower bound (~100 kg): below this, Comp-Bottom GT exceeds 10G limit. Upper bound (~3200 kg): above this, Roll-Wall dD exceeds dmax_shear = 81.28 mm. CB1500-50 K_comp = 795 lb/in, K_shear = 410 lb/in, dmax = 3.2 in [source: catalog_overview.md]. Tool uses binary search to find both boundaries [source: find_capacity_limit]. Standard: 20G/11ms saw-tooth per MIL-STD-810H Category 4 [source: formulas.md, selection_rules.md].

query: I only have 30 mm of deflection clearance above the rack. Mass is 800 kg with default mounts. Which CB part fits?
ground_truth: Deflection-constrained selection for M = 800 kg, default 6 bottom + 4 wall mounts, 30 mm clearance limit, 20G/11ms shock: the recommended part is the softest variant whose worst-case dD <= 30 mm AND passes 4-case shock analysis. Likely in the CB1400-15 to CB1400-20 region (K_comp ~1365-2650 lb/in) -- softer CB1400 parts (-25 and below) exceed the 30 mm clearance on Roll-Wall (shear direction has lower stiffness, higher dD). Standard applied: 20G/11ms saw-tooth per MIL-STD-810H Category 4 [source: formulas.md]. Caveat: a tighter clearance constraint than the isolator's own dmax forces a stiffer part than the unconstrained softest-valid-K selection -- transmissibility GT will be higher [source: selection_rules.md].

query: Tight 25 mm side clearance, rack is 1100 kg with 6 bottom 4 wall. What works?
ground_truth: Deflection-constrained selection for M = 1100 kg, 6 bottom + 4 wall mounts, 25 mm clearance, 20G/11ms shock: a 25 mm clearance is tight and requires a relatively stiff CB part. Likely the CB1400-10/-12 or CB1500-12/-15 region (high K_comp and K_shear so worst-case dD stays under 25 mm). Standard applied: 20G/11ms saw-tooth per MIL-STD-810H Category 4 [source: formulas.md]. Caveat: 25 mm side clearance is tight; the unconstrained softest-valid-K selection would give better isolation but with much larger dD [source: selection_rules.md].

query: Show me which CB1400 parts keep deflection under 20 mm for 850 kg with the standard mounting
ground_truth: Deflection-constrained selection for M = 850 kg, default 6+4 mounts, CB1400 series only, 20 mm clearance limit, 20G/11ms shock: only the stiffest CB1400 variants qualify -- likely just CB1400-10 (K_comp = 3515 lb/in, K_shear = 1801 lb/in). Worst-case dD ~19.8 mm on Roll-Wall (XZ shear), just under 20 mm. Other CB1400 parts (-12, -15, etc.) have worst dD > 20 mm because shear stiffness is lower than compression stiffness. Caveat: a 20 mm clearance is very tight -- only the stiffest CB1400 variant fits; transmitted G is higher (~8G worst case) than the unconstrained softest selection would give [source: selection_rules.md]. Standard: 20G/11ms saw-tooth per MIL-STD-810H Category 4 [source: formulas.md].

query: Pull the active CAD model and recommend a shock mount for it
ground_truth: Workflow: (1) extract_cad_data reads mass plus bounding box plus CG from the active SolidWorks assembly. (2) select_isolator runs the 4-case analysis using extracted mass with default 6+4 mounts and 20G/11ms shock spec. (3) Recommendation = softest CB part passing all 4 cases [source: selection_rules.md]. Standard applied: 20G/11ms saw-tooth per MIL-STD-810H Category 4 [source: formulas.md]. Caveat: CG height not verified explicitly -- if mass sits high on the rack, lateral cases may be underestimated [source: selection_rules.md].

query: I have a SolidWorks assembly open. What mount works for it with 8 bottom + 6 wall mounts?
ground_truth: Workflow: (1) extract_cad_data reads mass from active SolidWorks document. (2) select_isolator with extracted mass, n_bottom = 8, n_wall = 6 (heavy shelter rack config -- typical for systems above ~1500 kg) [source: selection_rules.md]. (3) Recommendation = softest valid CB part passing all 4 cases. Likely CB1500 or CB1700 family given the heavy mount count. Standard applied: 20G/11ms saw-tooth per MIL-STD-810H Category 4 [source: formulas.md].
